C-BROWSER-M1-1-AUDIT-REMEDIATION-2026083.Summary: Browser M1.1 Audit Remediation: Dedicated Real-Engine Gate, Safe CDP Arguments and Blink AX-to-DOM Resolution
C-BROWSER-M1-1-AUDIT-REMEDIATION-2026083.Problem: The applied M1.1 spike still runs the real Chromium integration test inside the ordinary correctness workspace test command, uses a fragile short CDP startup probe, interpolates untrusted ElementRef keys and input text into JavaScript source, and reconstructs a synthetic DOM-tag tree instead of returning the real Blink accessibility tree. These defects make the hosted correctness gate unreliable, violate browser capability semantics, and leave the documented AX-tree evidence unproven.

Goals.Goal: Move real Chromium acceptance into one explicit, required, feature-gated CI suite without running it from ordinary workspace correctness tests.
Make Chromium readiness bounded and robust with a 30-second deadline, complete bounded HTTP response parsing, early child-exit detection, and cleanup on failed startup.
Execute browser actions with Runtime.callFunctionOn and CDP arguments passed by value so node keys and input text can never alter JavaScript source.
Restore Accessibility.getFullAXTree semantics and bind actionable AX nodes to exact DOM targets through backendDOMNodeId and DOM.resolveNode.
Preserve document-revision staleness, capability authority, engine-neutral contracts, and truthful GRACE/ADR verification evidence.

Constraints.Constraint: Browser behavior remains in the browser plugin/provider; the kernel and logical browser contract remain engine-neutral.
Untrusted node keys and action payloads must not be concatenated into executable JavaScript source or selector source.
The real-engine test remains fail-closed when the dedicated CI gate cannot discover or start a supported browser.
Existing protected acceptance tests and M0/S0/S1 invariants must not be weakened, skipped, deleted, or rewritten to hide failures.
ElementRef actions must continue to reject page or document-revision mismatches before provider-side execution.
Only the new active change scope may be edited; shared GRACE projections are reconciled after fresh evidence.

NonGoals.NonGoal: Full production CEF embedding or the M1.2 browser provider process.
Changing the public logical browser capability contract or introducing browser-specific policy into the kernel.
Adding public-internet dependencies, live services, retries that hide flaky failures, or a second browser engine.

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: cargo test --workspace and the Correctness suite do not execute real_chromium_acceptance; the test is enabled only through an explicit real-engine feature and command.
A dedicated RealChromium CI suite runs exactly once as a named required Windows gate for pull requests and master, with the repository-owned script as its entrypoint.
Chromium startup uses a 30-second overall deadline, bounded complete readiness-response parsing, child-exit diagnostics, and kills/reaps the child plus removes temporary state on startup failure.

Input, click, submit, and focus actions resolve the exact backend DOM node and pass node/action values through CDP Runtime.callFunctionOn arguments by value; hostile quote and JavaScript payloads remain literal data.

query_document calls Accessibility.getFullAXTree, preserves Blink role/name/value and parent-child semantics within QueryBounds, and emits ElementRef keys that are resolved through DOM.resolveNode for exact action targeting.
Real Chromium acceptance proves safe hostile input handling, targeted input and click behavior, AX-to-DOM resolution, stale/nonexistent reference rejection, and renderer-crash containment.
Browser contract, browser spike, architecture/security, proving-slice, and GRACE verification evidence remain green with no unsupported or synthetic real-engine claim.

VerificationIntent.ExpectedEvidence: Fresh deterministic evidence shows the default workspace/correctness path excludes real Chromium, the dedicated Windows gate executes it once, malformed/hostile values cannot become script source, Blink AX nodes are tied to exact DOM nodes, and all existing invariants remain verified.

Assumptions.Assumption: The current applied M1.1 bundle is the baseline and there is no active overlapping browser change; this remediation supersedes neither the logical contract nor the M1.2 provider work.
The dedicated hosted Windows environment either provides a supported Chromium-compatible binary at the documented discovery path or provisions one before the fail-closed test runs.
GRACE graph and verification projections may receive a central delta only after implementation evidence passes and the user explicitly authorizes apply/archive.
